utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Due to technical problems here in the courtroom, we have a delayed start today. Good morning, sir. Welcome back to the courtroom. I have to remind you that the solemn declaration you made yesterday at the beginning of your testimony still applies. And Mr. Tolimir is continuing his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: {Witness answered through Interpreter]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yesterday we stopped when we were explaining the situation that you were explaining in the Bandera Triangle. I would like to ask you if, on the basis of everything that we said yesterday about the Bandera Triangle, if you were ever there. Were you ever in the Bandera Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have certainly been there twice; once to try to meet up with Mr. Zulfo, and the second time to try to relieve some colleagues that had been stopped during a patrol. They had been stopped by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you manage to reach some kind of agreement with the Muslims about UNPROFOR-Muslim relations in the Bandera Triangle? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not personally able to bring about any agreements. Mr. Karremans and perhaps higher-ranking officers were working on that. In any case, after having been detained for two or three days, we were able to return to our base. True freedom of movement, however, we did not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at D66 in the e-court, please. Could the electronic court please show D66. This is a report sent by Naser Oric, the commander of the Srebrenica Brigade, to the command of the 2nd Corps, where he says, in the second line - we can see the document now - he says, in the second line, I quote -- actually, we can start from the first line: "Due to the situation in the Podgaj village on 9th of January 1995, of which you were informed in a timely manner, the command of the 8th Operations Group has restricted the movement of the UNPROFOR forces in the broader region of Suceska and Podgaj. At about 1100 hours today the commander of the Dutch Battalion in Srebrenica ordered his patrols to enter the movement restriction area. In coordination with the commander of the 8th Operations Group respecting the agreement reached with the UNPROFOR liaison officer after the warning was issued not to move in the aforementioned area, the commander of the 281st Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade blocked all UNPROFOR patrols and is still keeping them blocked." Are you able to tell us whether this refers to you as the liaison officer and were you the one who reached this agreement with the commander of the operations group? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that this situation figured at the start of my period in the enclave. At that moment, we had the arrangement of a civil and a military liaison officer, because there were two of us, and there was a third person in addition to Mr. Rave and myself. That person eventually left. I think he was more involved in this process. I was present at one or two of these discussions. If I remember correctly, UNMOs were present as well. They were also trying to bring about freedom of movement in that area, and were similarly unsuccessful. And I believe that in that period somebody from UNPROFOR also tried to visit DutchBat. Whether it truly happened, I think it did, but I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: Did you take part in the talks in order to resolve the problems in the Bandera Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is yes, I was present at some of --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And was an agreement reached between the Muslim army and the UNPROFOR that the UNPROFOR does not enter the Bandera Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in the subsequent period, UNPROFOR provided indications that we should try to increase freedom of movement, and as a consequence, DutchBat carried out more patrols in that area. One of the results as a consequence of this was the hostage-taking of that group, and I believe I didn't see the document, but I remember that later indications arrived from UNPROFOR -- UNPROFOR provided indications that these operations should be scaled back and that there shouldn't be extensive patrols in the Bandera Triangle to bring about freedom of movement. So status quo, restricted freedom of movement, was accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document, D66 -- I'm sorry, thank you, Aleksandar. It's already been admitted, my assistant has told me. Are you able to tell us if you had received a written or an oral order from your superior command no longer to patrol in the Bandera Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any such written document, nor was I in that line of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at 1D362, 1D362. Thank you. We are now looking at 1D362. We are reading the first paragraph just below the Order. We don't have a translation, so this is a document by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, its 2nd Corps command from Tuzla, which is sent to the Srebrenica Operations Group, and it's addressed to the commander, Naser Oric. These are measures in relation to UNPROFOR, that is the heading of the document. I'm just reading the first paragraph of the order. Thank you. I quote: "The command of the Operations Group 8 will provide to the 2nd Corps command a detailed report with the date, time, place and type of impermissible activities by the Dutch Battalion of the UN in the area of responsibility of the 281st Light Mountain Brigade/Operations Group 8, Srebrenica." I end my quote. So my question is: Are you able to tell us, what are these activities that are not permitted that are referred to in this order?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing comes to mind now. It could have been the patrols.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you said that was addressed to Naser Oric. Can you tell me where I can find the name of Naser Oric in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If you look in the right-hand corner, it says "Urgent," and then underneath that, it says "OG 8, for the commander." He was the commander of Operations Group 8. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is the conclusion you are drawing from this document, but the name is not written here; is that correct? Just for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. For the transcript, I am saying that it is addressed to the commander of Operations Group 8. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Mr. President, there is no dispute from the Prosecution that Naser Oric was indeed the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just wanted to have it clear on the record. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question, on the basis of your previous answer, is: Did UNPROFOR take any kind of impermissible activity in the Bandera Triangle? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question is: As members of UNPROFOR, were you unwanted or people non grata in the Bandera Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an area where we were not welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at -- can we have this document 1D362 admitted, please? Aleksandar, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can the witness now look at 13 -- actually, 1D366. Can we show that document to the witness. Thank you. That is a document of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, by the command of the 2nd Corps, which was sent to deputy -- to assistant commanders for security of Operations Group 8 and it relates to movements by UNPROFOR members. I'm going to read the second paragraph. I quote: "In order to prevent these actions and occurrences --" meaning the movements of UNPROFOR -- "and for the purpose of protecting the units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the population, special purpose production, and other elements important for the defence of the country, it is necessary that all visits by members of UNPROFOR and other international foreign institutions and organisations to units and members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina be announced via the liaison officers at the corps command and that they be announced in advance." My question, on the basis of what I read, is this: Are you able to tell us, what is this special purpose production that they are protecting and what is its relevance to the Bandera Triangle? I didn't come across any references to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any additional information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you are being requested here to announce in advance each of your visits, and it says here because of special purpose production and other elements important for the defence of the country, they are protecting those, and that's why they say it is necessary that all visits by members of UNPROFOR and other international organisations, and so on and so forth, be announced in advance. Please, did UNPROFOR have any information that something was being produced or manufactured in the Bandera Triangle, such as weaponry or equipment? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just an inquiry, Mr. President, because we don't have a translation of this document. I'm just wondering if somebody can tell us whether this document refers to the Bandera Triangle in particular or at all or whether it's just a general document pertaining to the entire enclave. I note that the date appears to be 4 January. We have been dealing with the Bandera Triangle, but I just can't tell whether this document actually deals with the Bandera Triangle itself only, partially, not at all, or just the enclave. I don't know if the Defence has a position on that or whether they can tell us, based on their review of the document, since we don't have a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is in the same position. We don't know all the background and the content of this document. The witness is not able to give us additional information. What is it about, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In the beginning, I did say who wrote the document and that the document is titled, "Movement of members of the UNPROFOR, instruction, addressed to." This document refers to UNPROFOR, who is being banned from going to areas where special purpose production and other elements important for the defence of the country are being protected. And I'm asking the witness if he knows whether something was being manufactured there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This question is, sir, are you able to explain to the Trial Chamber what this special purpose production is?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a question to me or is it an explanation to the Judge? I thought it was the latter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, it is a question for you, Mr. Boering. Are you able to explain to the Trial Chamber what this special purpose production is? That was the question for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is this some kind of a special purpose production? Because it's called "special purpose production." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the name of military production, any kind of production; materiel, equipment, military equipment, used for this kind of production in NATO countries, including Holland?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in a factory?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Anywhere. It can be out in an open area as well. Anywhere. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the patrols that took place throughout the Srebrenica enclave did not discover any weapons-producing facilities. And, of course, one of their tasks was to seek out any facilities where such items could be produced inside a building or outside. One problem that we encountered in ascertaining where activities were being performed in buildings was that in house searches we had to be assisted by the police, so our mandate did not provide us with the full latitude to conduct house searches everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In view of this answer of yours, were you able to discover a weapons-producing facility in the Bandera Triangle if you were restricted from moving in that area? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the third paragraph. You see it in front of you. I'm going to read it. It says: "The corps command and the UNPROFOR liaison officer who is stationed at that location needs to coordinate positions about the procedure of announcing the movements and control by teams, crews, patrols, and others from the UNPROFOR force, with the commands of the brigades, battalions, and defence lines of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it's required that the movement of UNPROFOR is channelled and reduced to as few patrols as possible in places where they could possibly observe and gather intelligence data." So were you obliged, pursuant to this order, to announce in advance the movements of your patrols in these areas that were under the control of the Muslim army? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that with respect to the actual DutchBat patrols. I do remember that the UNMOs, when they actually wanted to enter the Bandera Triangle or that area, that they would submit a plan in advance and request permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Whose permission did they ask for, and was the Bandera Triangle a militarised or a demilitarised zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That permission was requested, if I remember correctly, at the weekly meetings we had with Naser Oric or Ramiz, his deputy, or Ekrem, the third man. The schedule of the week ahead was reviewed there, and whether the Bandera Triangle was militarised or demilitarised, as far as we could tell from outside, it was unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since the transcript is not written in the best possible way, would you kindly repeat whether the Bandera Triangle was a militarised or a demilitarised zone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no view of what actually took place in that area, but we didn't see any operations being performed from outside of that area. We couldn't see any such operations being performed with great military prowess, so it could have been a demilitarised area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Since you were obliged to announce your movement as members of UNPROFOR to military forces within that zone, and in view of the fact that they controlled your movement, were you then able to control them or to monitor them if you announced your movement a week ahead? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the case. And as I've indicated earlier today, the battalion leadership had decided to increase the patrols later in January.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As liaison officer, if you had to submit a report to the UNPROFOR command in Tuzla or Sarajevo and report to them whether that zone was militarised or demilitarised based on what you could observe, what would you have reported?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not submit any reports to Tuzla or Sarajevo as liaison officer. Karremans did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you Karremans' adviser; and what would you have advised him to report about whether Srebrenica was a militarised --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Whether Bandera Triangle ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: -- was a militarised or a demilitarised zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have advised him to try to get some insight in the Bandera Triangle and to carry out patrols there and to include that in the negotiations toward Tuzla and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. As this document has not been translated, I will read out the last three lines in the fourth paragraph, and they talk about controls on separation lines. And it says: "Military police and the Ministry of the Interior will carry out visual controls and ask for IDs of all persons from the UN complement." Now, tell us, please, what was your reaction to this decision taken by the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have no knowledge of this. I don't know whether that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever leave that zone? Did you exit or enter it? And were you then, on those occasions, asked for your IDs by the MUP or Ministry of the Interior police, or the military police? So when you went out of or came into the demilitarised zone.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember ever presenting an ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm running out of time, but could you please just answer the following question: If the command of the operations group Srebrenica - and Srebrenica was a demilitarised zone - actually worked or dictated the relationship within -- with the UNPROFOR within the demilitarised zone, could then that zone be considered demilitarised or were you actually under the control of the organs within -- the military organs within the so-called demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I remember is the restricted freedom of movement in the Bandera Triangle, and controls preventing them from moving ahead at a certain point. I don't have that impression and nothing comes to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We cannot dwell on this anymore. Can you just tell us, if you know, whether there was an agreement in place between the UNPROFOR and the BH Army on non-entry of the UNPROFOR into the Bandera Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said earlier today, after we stepped up the patrols later on in January and were blocked and taken hostage, I believe that subsequent to that, UNPROFOR issued instructions to accept the Bandera Triangle and its restricted freedom of movement for us. I did not see any documents to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know the observer, who was called Kingori, and was he in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him, and that was in Srebrenica. He was an UNMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before we move to the next topic, it may have gotten buried in some of the questions, but I believe General Tolimir had tendered 1D362, which was the document before the one he just used, and I don't know if he intended to tender 366, which is the one that he just finished up with. I do recall him tendering 362, but then he rolled right into another question so it may have gotten buried somewhere. So just before we move any further, just so there is no confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this reminder. I was waiting for tendering the current document by Mr. Tolimir. Are you tendering it? The Chamber has some concern --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President. We would like to tender it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is not in the position to admit these two documents into evidence. We don't know anything about the content. It is not only a translation issue. This witness couldn't say anything about the content. He doesn't know anything. He several times repeated, "I have no idea about it." And the questions you put in relation to these two documents to the witness were not answered in a way that we can receive these two documents into evidence. You may tender them with another witness, use them with another witness, but in that way we only can mark them for identification but not admit into evidence. They will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, document 1D00362 shall be marked for identification as D00141, while document 1D00366 shall be marked for identification as D00142. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This document, in its third paragraph, and I've read this out to the witness, it says that the corps command, would coordinate with the liaison officer of UNPROFOR, and this man was a member of the UNPROFOR, and he should be able to testify about this, and I have just heard him say that he had received an order from the command in Sarajevo not to go to Bandera Triangle, and I don't see why this document would not be or cannot be admitted into the evidence, because this witness is able to testify about it. He was a liaison officer and he was the person through whom actually all these arrangements about movements within the zone were done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, I have to interrupt you. The Chamber has ruled on that. Please carry on. No discussion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, sir -- could we please see P996, the so-called Kingori diaries. And could we pull up page 3 in e-court. Thank you. And I thank Aleksandar. You can see it on the screen before you now. And that's the fourth line, where Mr. Kingori says, "Control of movement towards Zepa (Carter agreement)." Now, please tell us what you know about the Carter agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, obviously we have no objection to the use of this document or any continued questioning along this line. I'd just ask perhaps if the witness could be given either an opportunity to at least have a moment to look at the document or have it placed in some kind of context for him, either by date or topic, just so we have -- or the witness has some idea what -- what this particular page of this journal reflects. That's all I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be helpful indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To assist the witness in order to give him -- in order to give him the opportunity to answer questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We've had Mr. Kingori as a witness here, and when asked why entry into Bandera Triangle was banned, and who had made the decision and on whose decision it was done, he answered that this was a way in which the Muslims protected people from leaving to -- from Srebrenica to Zepa, and then he mentioned the Carter agreement. And my question for you is: What do you know about the Carter agreement?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this time, nothing comes to mind about the Carter agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can -- does any other agreement come to mind? Can you recall any other agreement which regulated the UNPROFOR issue and its movement within the Bandera Triangle and movement from Srebrenica towards Zepa? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is not a huge issue but apparently it's an important issue to General Tolimir. I think he needs to be very careful when he's characterising another witness's testimony when he's examining a witness currently, and I think if we look at the record, it's clear that Colonel Kingori never connected the Bandera Triangle to the activities that are listed here on this document. I think the Trial Chamber will remember Colonel Kingori talking about OP Kilo and an OP in the south of the enclave, but he was careful to distinguish the Bandera Triangle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sorry, and I won't go any further, but there is mischaracterisation of the prior testimony that I think we need to be careful about. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, you may deal with that in re-examination. The question was quite clear: Can you recall any other agreement which regulated the UNPROFOR issue and its movement within the Bandera Triangle and movement from Srebrenica towards Zepa? This is a clear question. The witness should answer that. If you are able to answer that, please give us the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know nothing about agreements regarding the Bandera Triangle. As for discussions about movement between Srebrenica and Zepa, I remember that there were discussions about that, especially concerning smuggling operations, and that DutchBat tried to get more insight into that and indicated that they would be moving observation posts to improve their insight into that, and that gave rise to tensions with the Muslim leadership, who did not agree with the location of the new observation posts. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As Mr. Thayer, the Prosecutor, says that Kingori never mentioned control of movement, would you please read out the line, line 4, and read what it says in brackets for transcript purposes. Would you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The left side of the screen. I think Mr. Tolimir is referring to the fourth bullet point. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean, "Control of movement to Zepa, (Carter agreement)"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kingori spoke about that during his evidence, and I just want to point out that this document has already been admitted into evidence, and I thank Aleksandar for reminding me of that. Thank you as well. As for this illicit activities of the Muslims and the protection of the Muslims and the ban on movements of patrols, could we -- UNPROFOR patrols, could we now please show the witness document 65 ter 0696. That's a document produced by the BH Army, a report sent from Srebrenica on the 28th of April 1995, to the General Staff of the BH Army, personally to Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic. And I will repeat, while we wait for the document to show up, 65 ter 06696. 65 ter 06696, thank you. Thank you. Now we see the document in both versions, and I will read out the first paragraph, and I quote: "On the 27th of April, 1995, the command of the Dutch Battalion in Srebrenica began carrying out engineering work in order to set up an observation post in the Lozina village sector on their own -- of their own will. They made the decision to do so on their own. The setting up of an observation post in this area creates the preconditions for controlling the Srebrenica-Zepa corridor [road] which directly impedes the safety and secrecy of the transport of materiel and technical equipment which is delivered to Srebrenica in the customary manner." Please tell us, can you recall these activities of April? Because you were a liaison officer at the time. And what is this exactly about? What does this concern? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember them. They related to an effort by DutchBat to deploy more observation posts to have a clearer view of what was happening around the enclave, and this was part of a plan to improve the view of what was happening both within and outside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you prohibited from stationing or setting up a check-point in that sector, the sector of Lozina village? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present at all discussions about this because I had other duties as well, but I remember that the Muslims resisted, they objected, and exactly how setting up these new observation posts were negotiated, whether the location was adjusted as a compromise, I don't remember that. But I believe that new observation posts were placed in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what it was called, this observation post in the Lozina sector? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, that was Observation Post Kilo. It may have initially served as a temporary post, given the lack of clarity between both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you mean -- when you say "the parties," do you mean the BH Army and UNPROFOR or do you mean the warring parties? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean by that is between UNPROFOR and DutchBat or, rather, DutchBat and the Muslim authorities, whether these were, in fact, military people or a combination including the mayor of the enclave, I think it was a combination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to read paragraph 2, even though I thought I wouldn't. "UNPROFOR representatives do not accept our interpretation of the agreement on the complete cessation of hostilities reached between representatives of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the aggressor. In view of such a state of affairs, the liaison officer of the 28th Army Division Srebrenica requested an urgent meeting with representatives of the Dutch Battalion command. He met them twice on 28th of April, 1995, at 10 and 1600 hours, when he attempted invoking documents of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the 2nd Corps command in Tuzla to make it clear to them that the setting up of a new observation post was impermissible without a previous proposal to do so by the joint regional commission comprising representatives of UNPROFOR and the 28th Division commands, which also has to be approved by the joint central commission." My question is: The problem of weapons smuggling from one enclave to another, from one demilitarised zone into another, should that have been resolved in the manner proposed in this document at a joint meeting between the UNPROFOR representative and the command of the Division whose weapons were being smuggled? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Setting up these observation posts related to smuggling in general, including supplies. It also related to safety, having a view of what was happening outside the enclave. It didn't target smuggling alone; it was a combination of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, Mr. Tolimir has mixed two parts of this document while reading from it. He started with paragraph 2 of the document and then he moved to paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: That was the interpreter's error because we were not sure where Mr. Tolimir was reading from. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clarifies the situation. And Mr. Tolimir was reading very fast, and it's very difficult when you are reading so fast to catch everything for the interpreters. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am going to repeat the first paragraph that I read as the first one so that the interpreters could put it into the transcript. I quote, the very beginning of the document: "On the 27th of April, 1995, the command of the UNPROFOR Dutch Battalion in Srebrenica began carrying out engineering work in order to set up an observation post in the Lozina village sector. They made the decision to do so on their own. The setting up of an observation post in this area creates the preconditions for controlling the Srebrenica-Zepa corridor [road] and vice versa, which directly impedes the safety and secrecy of the transport of materiel and technical equipment which is delivered to Srebrenica in the customary manner." That was the first paragraph of the report that was sent to the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from Srebrenica. I apologise for reading fast, and I thank the Presiding Judge for helping me to put this correctly into the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: As representatives of UNPROFOR, were you duty-bound to inform the Armija where you would set up your observation post? And did you have the right to monitor the roads to check if there was any smuggling activity there; for example, the Srebrenica-Zepa road?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At DutchBat we assumed that we had that right. That's why we did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The activities of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army in preventing UNPROFOR from doing its job, were they illegal or were they in line with the demilitarisation agreement? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was an attempt to keep those smuggling routes open. It was an attempt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Boering, this was not the question. Were they illegal or were they in line with the demilitarisation agreement? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you to the witness. My question is: Is it clearly stated in this report that the Srebrenica-Zepa road that passes through the village of Lozina is used for the passage of materiel, technical equipment, and weapons that are being sent from Zepa to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at paragraph 3 of this document in the Serbian. This is the last one that we are looking at, on page 1. In the English, this is also the last paragraph -- actually, it's on page 2 in the English. First paragraph on page 2. Thank you. I quote -- you've already seen it. It's the last paragraph. "For our part we want to stress that the setting up of an UNPROFOR observation post in this locality would practically block the Srebrenica-Zepa corridor and prevent the transport of materiel and technical equipment arriving from Zepa to Srebrenica. Consequently, we need your instructions and suggestions on how to resolve this problem." My question is: Was -- were you prevented or banned from setting up an observation post in the village of Loznica in order to prevent the flow of materiel and equipment and weapons from continuing -- which was supposed to be part of your duties?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that DutchBat gave this matter a lot of thought. As for whether an observation post was, in fact, set up in that area, in those immediate surroundings, does not come to mind at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Actually, it's already been admitted as a Prosecution exhibit so I withdraw what I was going to say. The document has already been admitted. Can we now look at the reply by the command of the 2nd Corps to this question. Can we look at 65 ter 06700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you tendering the last document? It was admitted yesterday as a P document and it will be part of the internal memorandum of the Registry. Please carry on and put a question to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now show the witness 65 ter 06700.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see it on the screen. This is a document of the 2nd Corps of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, addressed to the command of the 28th Division of the land army, and that relates to the cessation of construction activities on the UN observation post. Can we look at paragraph marked with the number 1 of that order. I quote: "1. The 28th Army Division command, in cooperation with the Srebrenica municipal civilian structures, shall undertake all measures not to allow further construction work on the UNPROFOR observation post in the Soline [sic] village sector. "2. In all contacts with the representatives of the Dutch Battalion, we shall consistently adhere to the position that the location of observation posts, locations of observation posts, were agreed on at the level of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the UNPROFOR B and H command at the signing of the agreement on the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa and that any change in that respect must be verified at the same level." Thank you. I'm finished with the quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a correction for the record. At page 23, line 10, what I think I heard through my earphones was Soline. It didn't make it into the transcript but I think we can all agree that what's in the document from which General Tolimir was reading was the village of Lozina, which we've heard reference to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The accused said Soline.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you Mr. Thayer. My question is -- actually I meant to say the village of Lozina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: Do you know if the UNPROFOR and the UNPROFOR command in Zepa agreed with the Main Staff of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army and the units in the Srebrenica demilitarised zone about the places where they could set up observation posts and the places where they could not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not known by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think it's break time. We are over time already. We need the first break now and we will resume five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Boering, has your command in Tuzla or Sarajevo advised you as the UNPROFOR command in Srebrenica that you were not to continue building up the observation post in Lozina village? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this observation post ever established in Lozina village? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I delve into my memory, I believe that there was a temporary post in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what it means, what "temporary" means.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a post consisting of a vehicle and manpower positioned there for a period, for example, a week, and is not intended to remain there permanently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you obliged to announce to the Muslims in every particular instance that you were to go to the Lozina village to carry out these searches or checks, to check whether the materiel that was not, in fact, permitted to pass through be transported down that road? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any specific procedure for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we show the witness in e-court D65 -- that was marked by Mr. Franken -- to assist the witness in answering my questions. Thank you. Thank you. Now, you can see this map. Can you please show us where the observation post was at Lozina village, and was it the observation post that you started constructing or the one that was actually shut down after it was prohibited by the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you asking the witness to mark it on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps the witness can tell us which observation post was set up there from which they had control over the village of Lozina. Thank you. And if possible, perhaps the witness can mark it on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the Court Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's been a while. It was somewhere here in the southern section. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, on this stretch of seven kilometres of either side of the road that went from Zepa through Lozina to Srebrenica, was there a check-point on that stretch? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the road from Srebrenica to Zepa, so outside the enclave in the direction of Zepa, we did not have a DutchBat check-point. Conceivably, there was a Muslim check-point. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that in Lozina village? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in that area, so I haven't the foggiest idea of that. In this specific area, and let's say the subject matter of this check-point, my involvement was peripheral. I was certainly not the main operator aware of all the ins and outs. This was more the area of Franken and Karremans, and the company's commander of the actual area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you don't know anything about that, I will not insist.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 65 ter 065701 [as interpreted]. And I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This marked map will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D00143, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you please repeat the 65 ter number. I'm not sure if that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wanted 06701. 06701.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told there was a problem with the last document, the marking on the map, that was lost by the Registry. This is the map D65, and I would like to ask the witness to draw the circle again on this map because it was not saved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now it should be saved and received as D143. Was it fixed now? So we are waiting for 65 ter 6701.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, we see it before us. I will now read out what this document deals with. This is a document from the 2nd Corps command and it is addressed to the command of the 28th Division, and it says that instructions are requested for further action in connection with UNPROFOR's intention to set up an observation post in Srebrenica. And this relates to Lozina. And I will only read out the first paragraph and see what the corps has to say about this. And I quote: "1. The assertion made by UNPROFOR in Srebrenica that de jure it has unrestricted freedom of movement and can choose the sites for OS on the territory of the Srebrenica demilitarised zone is accurate. Agreement on the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa of 8 May 1993. "2. The assertion of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica is true that, based on the agreement on demilitarisation, they are duty-bound to prevent any attempt of uniformed personnel to military equipment and combat assets to enter --" The second paragraph, while we wait for the English version, I will just read it out. "The assertion of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica is correct; namely, that on the basis of the agreement on demilitarisation, they are required to prevent any entry attempt by persons in uniform, combat equipment, and weapons in demilitarised zone." Could we please scroll the page up a little bit, because I would like to quote the next portion. And then it says: "Bearing this in mind --" and then it says, under 1: "The problem --"and may I just add this is the next page in English, a new paragraph numbered as paragraph 1, and it says: "This issue should not be escalated to the level of the General Staff, BH command of UNPROFOR, because the unit of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica would in that way, be allowed sufficient time to set up an observation post."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... English translation, there is no further page, and if I compare the two versions in English and B/C/S, number 2, it seems to be quite different. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we just need to stay on page 1 in the English and I think that will take care of the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not -- it seems not to be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's the wrong document, actually, Mr. President. I think they've got the wrong document on the screen. I was following, on my hard copy, along with what General Tolimir was reading. And I'm looking at the screen and I think that's the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only the date is the same. Mr. Thayer, it is a P document, tendered yesterday by the Prosecution. Perhaps there was a wrong translation added to the original B/C/S version. That might be the explanation for this difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm just confirming the B/C/S is correct, the -- if we go to page -- I'm sorry, Mr. President, but if we could go to page 2 just to see what we have there in the English, just see that again, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please wait a moment, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What we can do ist that's clearly the wrong -- it's an incomplete or erroneous translation. I've got an English hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's the right translation but incomplete. It just stopped after the third line of paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. I have a complete translation in English. We can put it on the ELMO, if that helps, or at least hand it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That would be very helpful. One copy for the witness, please, and another copy on the ELMO, please. Mr. Tolimir, we have this document in the English translation now on the ELMO and you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I just wanted to read out paragraph 1, below the interceding paragraph between 3 and 1: "Do not bring this problem to the level of the army General Staff, UNPROFOR's BH command, because this would give the UNPROFOR unit in Srebrenica ample time to set up an observation post." And my question for the witness is as follows: Since the superior command in Tuzla understood clearly that UNPROFOR was right in what they were saying, and we saw that in the first paragraph, my question to you is why was it that you did not insist on being allowed to proceed with the setting up of the observation post in Lozina village? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interpreting this for myself, item 1 of this document, which is disappearing now --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking you to interpret this document. Just please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, it refers to an assumption of DutchBat in Srebrenica, and there is no agreement from Tuzla or Sarajevo on this subject. So item 1, the assertion made by UNPROFOR in Srebrenica, the first line, indicates to me that it's a matter of interpretation by the unit in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Boering, Mr. Tolimir put to you the following question: Why was it that you did not insist on being allowed to proceed with the setting up of the observation post in Lozina village? That was the question. Have you an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why did you not insist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I was peripherally involved in this subject was not an operator present at all meetings, so this could be a perfectly good question, but not to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, continue please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Since Witness does not know the answer, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, that was tendered and admitted yesterday through the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Could I please see the texts again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Boering, you touched something on this machine and that was the moment it disappeared. It was the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have it on the screen. Mr. Boering, do you want to add something in respect to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't want to add anything. I'm happy to be seeing the transcript of the case in front of me again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now you have the transcript. Okay. Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We've already spent a lot of time on this so I have no further questions about this topic. Let's move on to the next group of questions. In view of the fact that Muslims in the area of Bandera Triangle conducted some illicit activities and that in Lozina village that was the case too, where they publicly said that there was a transport -- that weapons were being transported from Srebrenica to Zepa, did the UNPROFOR command in Srebrenica inform the -- its superior command of this?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were weekly or daily reports from DutchBat to the superior command, and all matters that were known or suspected were reported. So I assume that matters such as suspected arms smuggling was reported as well. But confirmed transport, smuggling of arms, as far as I know, we didn't actually identify those.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of these impermissible activities and no overview of the activities, did UNPROFOR try to assess what were the intentions of the operations group in Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must undoubtedly have happened. And as far as I remember, that related in part to smuggling operations and the objective was to get something of an impression of that, and DutchBat tried to carry that out, and we were able to do that to some extent because our own logistics was no longer optimal either; fuel shortages and the like. So we were no longer able to operate extensively everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since these are activities from January 1995 and then April 1995, were you restricted because of the fuel quantities from carrying out your full duties in controlling the demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say from March and April, we -- our fuel supply was reduced, the supplies to the enclave were reduced due to lack of clearances issued and, as a consequence, we weren't able to operate as much with vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we have to finish the testimony of this witness today. I think you are going around and around the same topic. If you want to raise other matters in your cross-examination, you should consider that, to do that as soon as possible. We have lost a lot of time this morning by repeating the same questions, and once you said, "I'm running out of time." That is perhaps because of some repetition, we have to observe. If you want to raise other matters, deal with other issues, you should do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: Were you able to reach other points other than the ones that were located in the Bandera Triangle that we were discussing? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm doing my best to understand your question, but I'm not entirely successful. I would say that we had freedom of movement in the enclave except for the Bandera Triangle, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Boering. We are not going to talk about that anymore. I would like to see D67 in e-court, and then I'm going to put questions to you on the basis of facts that are going to be evident from this document. Thank you. We see a document here from the General Staff of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 13th of July 1995, after the fall of the enclave, to the president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, as an interim report, listing all their military activities in the Srebrenica and Zepa zones. In paragraph 2, line 1, the only one, it says: "Specifically, the following has been done for Srebrenica and Zepa." And then the first bullet point: "To start with, lethal assets and materiel and technical equipment were brought in on foot in fairly small quantities. "2. 17 helicopter flights were carried out in each of which a helicopter was hit." And later we'll see what was brought in on these helicopters. "3. In this way we transported a number of seriously wounded injured and brought in and took back 15 from Srebrenica and five from Zepa, men who are graduated from the wartime officers' college. "4. In preparation for a future operation to link up the enclaves, we brought in and took back four brigade commanders, two brigade chiefs of staff, and the 26th Division Chief of Staff. The Division commander, who was meant to go on the next helicopter flight, did not return after the final flight ended tragically. Naser remained." My question is: If you remember, you said that you did not see Naser Oric after February. This is something you said in the examination-in-chief. Was this the period when he left and could not return anymore? Is that the period in which these officers were in the territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina in order for the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves to be linked up at some point in the future with the corps? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those are several questions at once. Let me start with the first one. Sometime at the end of February, possibly, Naser Oric was discovered to have left. Where he actually was was kept secret. We suspected that he was in Tuzla. Whether at that point operations were in progress to connect or link up Zepa and Srebrenica, I don't know about that. I did not hear or see any information about that. I was aware that smuggling was taking place between the two enclaves, and the staff, including the mayor of Srebrenica, sometimes stayed in Zepa. So there was a link between Zepa and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to say whether the UNPROFOR command in Srebrenica at any point got any information that would indicate that the demilitarised enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica wanted to link up and wanted to link up with their corps, the home unit in Tuzla and Kladanj? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the next page of this document in the Serbian. And in the English it's already on this page, if we can just scroll up a little bit and then continues in -- on the next page, and then we can see what has been brought in from -- of the weapons. I think this is sufficient of a question for the witness. Thank you. My question is: These weapons and these reports, do they indicate that the Muslim army was preparing for some combat assault actions, and did UNPROFOR have any information about these assault actions that were being launched from the demilitarised zones? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no immediate answer to that. There were regular reports of breakouts from the enclave in the direction of Serbia, but as for actually being involved in the planning or being notified that the activities were taking place, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at 65 ter 040333. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the number. I'm not sure if we have the correct number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 04033. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: While we are waiting, I'm going to say, because there is no English, this is a document that the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska sent to the commander of the Main Staff about activities of the enemy in relation to the units of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a hard copy, English translation. I might suggest that we do the same as we did with the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is there no English translation in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I don't know if there is. There wasn't one listed in the defence list. Doesn't appear that there is one in e-court, but I have one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It should be put on the ELMO. The Chamber would appreciate if the translation could be uploaded in e-court. Mr. Gajic. Mr. Tolimir, your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I just indicated what the document was about. I'm going to quote a part of the document and then I'm going to put a question to it. This document was signed by General Tolimir and sent to the commander of the Main Staff and the 65th regiment because of the activities directed at the Main Staff and the regiment. It states here: "On the 23rd of June of this year, at 0200 hours, a unit of approximately 300 soldiers headed out from Srebrenica, led by Ibrahim Mandic, the commander of the 281st Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade, Veis Sabic, the commander of the 284th Light Mountain Brigade, and his deputy Semso Salikovic and a guide man called Zoran Cardakovic, a Muslim. The unit's task was to insert itself that same day at approximately 2200 hours into the general sector of Ruzine Vode, Han Pijesak municipality. This group is equipped with automatic weapons, with a couple of 60 millimetre mortars, and some rocket-propelled grenades." Thank you. Please, my question is: Did you have any information that groups were infiltrating themselves from demilitarised zones, from Srebrenica to Zepa, in groups of 300 or so soldiers and that they were led -- being led to carry out various assignments in the depth of the defence of the Army of Republika Srpska, as we can see on this -- in this information from the Main Staff? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The last paragraph, the fourth paragraph in the Serbian on this page, can we scroll up, please, states: "Also on the 23rd of June of this year, in the evening hours, a company of 120 soldiers --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We are unable to see the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the witness and now of the Court Usher, we will see it soon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "-- commanded by Zehrudin Jasarevic was sent from the composition of the Manoeuvre Brigade for a rotation to the sector of Jovino Brdo that will last five days and during which time they are to perform reconnaissance in the direction of Jeskovik [phoen] and the Peruca hydroelectric power plant in the Skelani municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is, did you have information that there was a Manoeuvre Brigade in Srebrenica and that they were carrying out actions in relation to Serbia and in relation to the hydroelectric power plant, which at that time was a key industrial facility, as it is now? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at 1D27, please. Thank you. Can we look at page 2 of this document. This is a document of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina command of the 28th Division, that it sent to the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. Can we look at page 2 of document, please, where the information is confirmed that they are also sending Mr. Tursunovic to Zepa. If you look at the second paragraph on this page, where it says: "Apart from the other measures, I have decided to send to Zepa part of the company sabotage and reconnaissance platoon, a unit attached to the staff, and the commander of the 281st Light Mountain Brigade, Major Zulfo Tursunovic." Can you tell us whether you knew anything about the departure of Tursunovic from Srebrenica to Zepa and his frequent trips to that area in order to guide the activities of the sabotage and reconnaissance platoon? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to page 1 of this document, please, at the very beginning. We are talking about the month of June - it's on the screen already - where it says in the document, I quote: "The problem of members of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and civilians leaving the Srebrenica and Zepa safe areas in the direction of Tuzla, Kladanj and Serbia, have been present since the first days of demilitarisation of this area." I'm going to skip a part and then I'm going to read line 15 to you of this first paragraph. This is five rows above this number, about the division command order, and that sentence states: "However, in the summer months it is as if some unknown wave flows through the people, suddenly creating a euphoria that the best solution is to leave for Tuzla. This literally causes waves throughout the entire area and the majority of people are then ready to leave." In view of this, and the fact that you said yesterday that they were not going to Tuzla voluntarily, can you say if you can tell from this document whether this was a problem that was there throughout the whole demilitarised period in the safe area, this departure of people going towards Tuzla and Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that the population was leaving in small groups for Tuzla or Kladanj. I was also aware that it was a dangerous stretch. I remember that in the period from March to June food and medical supplies seriously deteriorated so that the population figured out that prospects were grim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did UNPROFOR have reports that the civilians from the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves kept crossing over illegally to the territory under the control of the Muslim Federation, to Tuzla, Kladanj, Sarajevo, and so forth, and that some of them even tried to flee to Serbia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was clearly happening, and there were reports, for example, by the mayor of Srebrenica that things were tense among the locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If civilians throughout this period after 1993, when it was demilitarised, up until they left the enclaves, continued taking this trip, crossing dangerous territory, does this actually contradict your statement that they were not willing to leave, that they did not leave there willingly but were, rather, forced to? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your answer, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to figure out the question in my own mind. Ultimately, the population that left the enclave in convoys boarded the buses and, in my view, at that point those people had no other option because no supplies were available to meet their primary needs, and the same factor had motivated people to leave the enclave at previous points in time, so a form of voluntary departure, you could describe it as that, but forced by circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to page 2, please, of this document so that I can show you, if you did not remember it, and I'm referring to the passage that I quoted earlier about Major Zulfo Tursunovic who was supposed to prevent those people who were trying illegally to leave Zepa and go to Kladanj or Tuzla. So my question is: Did even Muslims prevent those Muslims who were trying and wanted to leave the enclaves? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have happened in that manner. To -- this was to have the enclave continue existing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to read out the penultimate sentence of this document. And this document was drafted by the Muslim side, not the Serb side. And it says: "A sabotage platoon of the company will, in cooperation with the police of the 285th Light Mountain Brigade, in identifying such people, arresting them and forcibly returning them to Srebrenica." And the last sentence: "We are of the opinion that the command of the 2nd Corps, in cooperation with the other authorities, should undertake more severe repressive measures against all persons leaving the zone." I'm not going to read any further. End of quote there. But my question would be this: Did even Muslims take repressive measures to prevent people from moving out of the demilitarised zones of Zepa and Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is apparent from this report drafted by Ramiz, Naser's deputy, this was policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking about the policy. I'm asking you whether you, as a member of UNPROFOR, had received such reports that the civilians were actually wanting to leave the demilitarised zones and move on to the areas under the control of the Bosnian Federation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that people I spoke with, whose prospects were grim, mentioned that they were considering leaving. Measures as described in this report were not reported to us, or in any case not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In other words, you did have such knowledge because you just told us that you had occasion to talk with people who had a grim view of the situation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to tender this document into evidence, unless it's already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D00144, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the previous document, 65 ter 4033 is not in evidence yet. Are you tendering it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received and we are hoping that the Prosecution will upload the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be received as D00145, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, yes, it will now be marked, not pending translations but pending uploading the translation. Then it will be an exhibit. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we now pull up in e-court 1D191. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is a document confirming the information we saw a little earlier, that sabotage units were being sent to take action against the Main Staff. Here we see this is a document from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, sent to the command of the 2nd Corps and the 28th Division, and it is sent as a combat report. And there it says: "Pursuant to an order from the representative of the commander of the 28th Division of Srebrenica, Major Ramiz Becirovic, strictly confidential, number 01-127, from 1995, dated 20th June 1995, on taking measures to conduct sabotage operations in order to inflict losses on the aggressor, personnel and materiel losses, and in the overall attempt to push back the Chetnik forces from Sarajevo." And now they number a number of -- they list a number of groups there. Can we please scroll this document a bit up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I don't see this document on your list of documents to be used during cross-examination. And in addition, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if there is a translation that the Defence has to assist the witness. I'm not sure if there is one available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. Mr. Gajic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we put documents -- as soon as we receive a translation of a document, we enter it in e-court. For this particular document, we have as yet received no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, it's not on the list of documents to be used with this witness. Mr. Tolimir, put your question to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Did you have information about sabotage terrorist groups being sent, led by Zulfo Tursunovic, from Srebrenica via Zepa to the Main Staff? And did you ever receive any such information from anyone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that Zulfo was active, and also that he was pressuring people in the Bandera Triangle, and that he frequently performed operations outside the enclave, but this was more general.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show another document from the same period, from June 1997, sent from the army of BH, that's document 1D356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have an English translation yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We haven't received it yet. We have requested a translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As we have no English translation, I will only read out the first paragraph under the date: "In the morning hours on the 26th of June, 1995, our forces from the Srebrenica area attacked and set on fire Visnjica village. According to unconfirmed information, Chetniks suffered losses among the civilian population." My question is this: Did you -- or were you ever informed about an attack launched from the enclave in Srebrenica on Visnjica village, which was outside the enclave to the west and that is exactly the area where your movement was restricted? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In contacts with Momir Nikolic in Bratunac, he regularly mentioned incidents of outbreaks from the enclave by Muslims, describing the losses. It's perfectly possible that this was reported to us, but it isn't fresh in my memory at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have this document admitted into evidence? That's 1D356. And in the meantime --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber has a problem with receiving that document. You have only put one question to the witness and he said, "It is perfectly possible that this was reported to us, but it isn't fresh in my memory at this time." I think there is no authentication by the witness about this document, we don't know any details about the document. We have a big problem to receive it at this point in time. You may use it with another witness and, especially as we have no translation, we don't know anything about it. Wait, please, I'm still talking. Your request to admit it is denied. Now we have another document on the screen. Please go ahead. Still the same. I'm sorry, I was mistaken. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would now like to pull up D52.
