That's a document that has already been admitted, and I would like to talk with the witness about this because he said that he didn't know that a village on the very border of the enclave had been torched. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we see that document, that's D52, another report from the command of the 2nd Corps of the BH Army of the 8th of July, 1995, when it was sent to units as information on combat results of the units and commands of the 28th Ground Army Division. Would you please just take a look at the first bullet point below the first paragraph. It says: "60 Chetniks were liquidated," so on and so forth, what was captured, and then it says: "In the village of Visnjica, large quantities of ammunition were seized but the soldiers were exhausted and could not remove all of it, so it was destroyed, as were all the facilities that the aggressor could use for military purposes." Thank you. End of quote. Now, you said that you had a meeting with Nikolic, and he might have mentioned this, but did you also have a meeting with Mr. -- a gentleman from the Milici Brigade regarding this same issue? And you mentioned this gentleman as a man by the name of Sarkic, and you said that you had two meetings with this person. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having dealt with Sarkic about this. I met with him once in early January at the introduction, at the very start of my deployment, and later on at the very end, upon my departure for Kladanj, he was present there. In between, I did not speak with him. All our dealings concerning the VRS either went through Vukovic or, ordinarily, they would go through Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In other words, you didn't know anything about your command having any information that a village to the west of the demilitarised zone had been torched in the area not far from the Bandera Triangle. It was some six kilometres from the separation line and Bandera Triangle.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, reports regularly arrived of shooting and combat, so it was known that activities were taking place in that region. The details of these operations, however, were not known, especially six kilometres away. It must have been audible to observation posts and must have been reported, but an actual description of what was happening in that village was not available to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now see 2806 in e-court, please. My apologies. Actually, we need 1D364 now, thank you. 1D364. Thank you. Here we have the document before us. It was also from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, its 2nd Corps, and in June - in other words a month before the events in the enclave - this document was sent to the commander of the 28th Division, of land forces, and the command of the 285th Light Brigade, and it goes on to read as follows: "Our congratulations on the successful completion of your combat operations which have significantly contributed to a successful completion of the operation to lift the blockade of Sarajevo and where you have inflicted heavy losses on the aggressor in the fight for the ultimate and final liberation of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the destruction of the Serbo-Montenegrin fascists." That is what it reads in this document, signed by the commander, Sead Delic. And then it goes on to say: "In the next period you are to comply with the orders issued so far. Prepare your plans for active combat at the appropriate time. Orders for those combat operations shall be forwarded to you from us or the BH Army Main Staff." Now, in view of what I've read, did you have any information that, in the month of June - in other words, a month before the enclave fell - in late June and later, Muslim forces were conducting active combat operations, as it says in this document, against the rear lines of the Serbian army? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were aware that activities were taking place from the enclave to relieve the burden from Sarajevo. And that was indicated regularly through our contacts with, in part, the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, keeping an eye on the clock for this witness, but also for future witnesses, we've said it before and I'll say it again, that it is not contested, in fact it's part of the Prosecution's case and has been from the beginning of this trial and previous trials, that the Muslim forces operating from within the Srebrenica enclave had, as part of their objective, tying down VRS troops as a way of drawing VRS resources away from the Sarajevo front. That is not contested. And I think I see from the cross-examination list of documents a number of documents - I don't know if there are a lot more - in this line of questioning, but again, it's not in contest, we could probably agree with the Defence, as we do, I think, on 99 per cent of their documents, that there will be no objection from the Prosecution to tendering them, whether it's by way of a bar table motion later or some other mechanism, but to just simply try to save some time and avoid going over these same uncontested issues, I would urge the Defence to look at that, especially with this witness, for whom we have a limited amount of time, but also in the future. Again, we are always available to do that; it is not contested in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Chamber would like to invite the parties to negotiate if it would be possible to reach an agreement about these facts. Indeed, that would help the Defence and the Chamber to know what we are talking about. The Chamber is concerned a bit about the time. It's the last hearing day of this year before the winter recess. I would like to ask Mr. Tolimir about your estimation of the remainder of cross-examination. You have used more than four and a half hours up to now. We have only three-quarters of an hour left. The Prosecution will need some time for re-examination. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not yet, Mr. President, and I doubt that we will have any, based on the way things are going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That will be very helpful, especially for Mr. Tolimir. Have you any idea if you will be able to finish the cross-examination today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm going to try to finish, and I thank Mr. Thayer for allowing us time to be able to complete the cross-examination of this witness by the end of the day today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We adjourn and resume at 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We tried to have a shorter break but we were not successful because of technical problems again. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In order to start with the footage right away, we can look at it right away, we don't need to lay down the foundation, and then we can move to questions. If we can look at P991 from 46.24 to 48, and if the witness can carefully look at the footage, pay attention to what the speakers are saying. Yesterday we actually had the transcript of this footage and we went over it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Boering, are you able to say if this is the first meeting that you and Mr. Karremans had with General Mladic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the first meeting with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you remember when the meeting was held, what time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meeting was on 11 July, I believe in the course of the afternoon, at Fontana.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this a meeting that was requested by General Mladic or by General Karremans? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me this question yesterday several times, and then I indicated that at this time I don't clearly remember that. In any case, there was some contact with Petar, the interpreter present in Bratunac, about this meeting. I thought about it some more last night. Conceivably we sought contact via Petar and, through this interpreter, this proposal at this time was made. So I think it was a combined event, perhaps first at our request and then accepted and subsequently requested by Petar. That's what comes to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Boering. Yesterday you also said that before this meeting, Colonel Karremans spoke with Nicolai. At this meeting, did he tell General Mladic what orders he received from General Nicolai and the command, as he put it, for Bosnia-Herzegovina? Thank you. The UNPROFOR command for Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He indicated, as conveyed in this video, that the intention was to leave the enclave, both DutchBat and let's call them the refugees. And the objective was to bring this about in the most appropriate possible way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to resolve this situation at the Potocari base, did you need the help of the Army of Republika Srpska to which you were directed by General Nicolai, according to what Karremans said?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we covered this topic in detail yesterday, I'm not going to go back to it. Can we now go back to your statement. This is page 4, paragraph 6, and this is the 65 ter number 06703. We will be looking at your statement now, the 65 ter number 06703. I would like to look at page 4, please, paragraph 6. And we can see that sixth paragraph in the Serbian. Can we also see it in the English, please. This is page 5 in the English. Thank you, Aleksandar. This is page 5, paragraph 2. You say, line 4, I'm quoting. Line 4: "During this night, Karremans and I held talks with the Muslims. Karremans promised the Muslims air support on that occasion. I suspect that the Muslim fighters decided that night that their position was untenable and that they would have to flee." My question is: Were you with -- were you alone with Colonel Karremans during these talks or were there any other persons who attended this meeting with the Muslims? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other people present, both from the Muslim side and for DutchBat. If I remember correctly, Sergeant Major Rave was also present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My next question is: Who was interpreting for you during this conversation that you had with the Muslims? Who translated what Mr. Karremans was saying? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect that it was Hasan, the interpreter who was ordinarily present in the PTT building. I can't think of his surname just now, but he's known.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to remember what Mr. Karremans told the Muslims that night in your presence and the presence of the interpreter Hasan Nuhanovic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember something about a commitment of massive air support, if the attack on the enclave continued by the VRS or, in fact, took place on the part of the VRS, and that would happen -- it was supposed to happen in the early morning hours, and that would be a massive attack, and people would need to take care for their -- to watch their own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: When you said "people," did you mean Muslims, the Muslims had to take care of their own security, their own safety?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "safety," I mean that you need to try to avoid getting hit by bombs that drop. And that held true both for our own DutchBat members as for the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the zone that needed to be evacuated indicated for the safety of Muslim members and UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that there was an area and there were borders, but the details are not fresh in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if you remember if Colonel Karremans spoke about massive bombardment of that area and that sector that he indicated? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned that. I think I explained that a few sentences earlier, about massive air support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's see what the Muslim representative said about that and what this translator said, Hasan Nuhanovic. Can we look at 1D137, now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you tendering the OTP statement of this witness, 65 ter 6703? I think you used it already yesterday but I'm not sure if you tendered it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, we would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it will be received as Exhibit D00146. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the e-court now to show 1D137, please. Sorry, I made a mistake. I actually need D137, without this 1 in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to appear on the screen, I'm going to say that this is a transcript of a conversation which was shown in a documentary film on Radio Television Serbia, on the 9th of July, 2010. I am reading this text in the second paragraph -- actually, the first paragraph says: "On the 10th of -- on the evening of the 10th of July, a meeting between the Dutch Battalion commander and representatives of the 28th Division was held in the post office building in Srebrenica. Hakija Meholjic, member of the Srebrenica War Presidency from 1993 to 1995." And now they are quoting the transcript of what was said in that programme: "In the meantime, Karremans arrived requesting a meeting. I told him, five more minutes, so we can first agree on everything ourselves because we have no reason to trust you anymore. We arranged everything, then we received him for a talk and he said that NATO informed him that a death zone has been set around Srebrenica for tomorrow at half past five. Everything that moves on two, four, or a hundred feet, or on a hundred wheels, or on one wheel or on two wheels, will be destroyed, that it will be destroyed." My question is: Do you remember whether Mr. Karremans said this in the way that Hakija Meholjic, the member of the Srebrenica War Presidency, conveys it here?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was stated literally that way, but the gist corresponds well with what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is: Did what Mr. Karremans announced actually take place; and if it did not, why did it not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it didn't happen en masse, and it didn't take place in the morning but later in the afternoon. And why it didn't happen? Extensive research has been conducted on that, many, many times, but that exceeds my scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what you know about the research that has been conducted into why the air-strikes did not happen? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that could become a very long answer. I derive most of the information from the reports to which you have access as well. Given the time pressure, I don't think it's relevant for me to elaborate on all that off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether NATO had a green light to bomb the positions of the Republika Srpska in and around Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any concrete information for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether NATO, when it announced that they would conduct air strikes, actually took sides in this conflict between the Muslims and the Serbs in Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that the actual support that took place was biased. It was a situation where their own troops were dealing with VRS units and these forward air controllers were under fire. So it wasn't bias; it was self-defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, does self-defence occur at the point of attack or subsequently? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since Colonel Karremans announced on the 10th that there would be air-strikes, he announced it on the 10th, that the air-strikes would follow in the early morning hours on the 11th, does this constitute self-defence if it is already announced ahead of time? Or would self-defence actually be considered self-defence if it happened once an attack occurred, or subsequently? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans did mention on the evening of the 10th that this bombing would take place if ongoing attacks were conducted that constituted attacks. And if you're under attack, you're entitled to defend yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at what the interpreter, Hasan Nuhanovic, who interpreted all that, let us hear what he had to say. "The Serbian side was given an ultimatum to withdraw by 0600 hours to their starting positions, in other words Zeleni Jadar, to go back six kilometres or they would be bombarded at 0600 hours." He says that "the number of aircraft that will come for air-strikes, they told me, would be between 40 and 70. That is what was -- what has been said." Now, this is what Hasan Nuhanovic said during the interview and this programme of the 10th of July, 2010. So my question is who was it who gave this green light for the bombing?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the accused please repeat his question. We did not understand him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters asked to repeat the question. I only see the question, "So my question is who was it who gave this green light for the bombing?" Was that your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My question was who issued the ultimatum to the -- to Republika Srpska; was it NATO or the UNPROFOR? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Boering.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of who issued the ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mr. Karremans mention this ultimatum of by 0600 hours? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it as follows: After this meeting, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans left for Potocari while I remained behind in Srebrenica. So what happened was that in Potocari, after Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans returned, was not -- I didn't observe that, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The UNPROFOR or NATO, by issuing an ultimatum to one of the warring parties, would that constitute taking sides, and would that shift the balance of forces? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think the witness has explained his position very clearly. He spoke about self-defence. You should not repeat the question. We have not so much time. We are approaching the end of today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would now like the witness to be shown again the statement D14, the witness statement that was 65 ter 60 -- 6703. What we would like to see is paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is D146.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we then please have D146 in e-court. And I would like the witness to be shown paragraph 6, on page 4 in Serbian and page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 in Serbian, in the first line, the last three words: "The captain out there had received information, a message that we had to establish definitively where the Serbs were located within the enclave. Only after the presence of Serbian fighters had been definitely confirmed and after positive identification of their presence and use of weapons would air support be given." My question is this: Who issued this assignment to Captain Groen, and why did they have to know the exact location of the Serbs, and did they have to engage them in order for air support to follow? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that this assignment was issued by Captain Groen or by Karremans. So there had to be an actual threat to be allowed to issue air support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did UNPROFOR soldiers, in keeping with this request from Captain Groen, have to locate the tanks of the VRS, the Republika Srpska army, and establish at the time that those tanks were actually firing in order for the air support to come? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think you could express it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. During the examination-in-chief you said that you couldn't recall the name of the lieutenant who was in charge of forward air controllers of UNPROFOR. Could you tell us, please, was it Lieutenant Egbers who was in charge of forward air control of UNPROFOR, and did he subsequently take any action in order to locate the targets of Republika Srpska to be able to guide the NATO air-strikes? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the actual execution of forward air controls was certainly not performed by Lieutenant Egbers. He may have provided instructions, but that was not observed by me. It was outside my field of observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you tell us the time you will need for concluding your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will conclude it within the time frame that you tell us we have, but I would just like to remind this witness that he was present there. Now, let's take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop. We are at the end of today's hearing and now I'm asking you how much time you need to conclude your cross-examination. That's a question to you. We are at the end of today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If you allow me, I would have an additional four to five questions, and I should be able to conclude my cross-examination by 1400. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please go ahead. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please take a look at line 4, paragraph 7, of your statement, on page 4 that we have before us. And you say there the following: "I went to confer again with a few Muslim administrators who communicated Serb positions to me. Every time DutchBat soldiers went to look at these positions, they were fired upon by the Serbs." Does this indicate that you too were involved in locating Serb targets and that you asked information from Muslim fighters to that effect? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did indeed do this, so in my view, that happened earlier, not on that day. In my view, it took place the day before. So I suspect that it happened before our meeting where Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans mentioned the massive air support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You begin this paragraph with the words "the next day," and that is why I asked you whether this was on the 11th, on the day when the positions of the VRS were under air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression is that this request or activity on my part with respect to the Muslims so that they could invoke the smoking-gun principle was on the previous day or on the day that we had that meeting in the evening with Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans. So it was probably on the 9th, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, was my question fairly put, and I only actually posed my question based on what you said there, that it was on the next day that Karremans had talks with the Muslims. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm gradually beginning to lose my power of concentration. I'm having trouble understanding this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir was referring to the beginning of that paragraph, "The next day there was no air support at the agreed time." And he wants to know the time frame, the subsequent events, when all that happened, especially he was asking you at which day you had the talks with the Muslims together with Karremans. If you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The conversation with the Muslims was in the evening of 9 July, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did Karremans then announce NATO air-strikes for the 10th or for the 11th? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the next day. If the conversation with the Muslims took place about the massive air support on the 9th, then the previous afternoon or morning was when the conversation took place with the Muslims about the smoking-gun principle, but exact days, it was a succession of events. Because in the morning of the 10th, no air support was forthcoming, my impression is that the enclave fell on the 10th. That's the way I've got it in my mind at this time but my power of concentration is eroding by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that, and I will not insist on this any longer, in view of the difficulties you're having, and it could happen to any one of us. Now, since we can no longer discuss matters that you have difficulty recalling at this point in time, let me just ask you quickly whether the assignment that Captain Groen received and forwarded to the air forward controllers, was it -- did it have to be met? In other words, did the tanks have to be found and did they have to be found with the so-called smoking-gun principle, and was that the condition for the air support to follow?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We will leave this topic since you don't know. But now could we see P1203. My apologies, P1202. My apologies to e-court. Page 1, P1202. While we are waiting for it to come up, we can see it in the Serbian language and, for the transcript, let me say that this is a document drafted by the command of the Drina Corps on the 2nd of July and forwarded to brigades as an order to prevent Muslim operations, and I will just read paragraph 1: "As part of an all-out offensive against Republika Srpska territory, the enemy has carried out attacks with the limited objective against the DK units. We believe that in the coming period the enemy will intensify offensive activities against the DK area of responsibilities, mainly in the Tuzla-Zvornik and Kladanj-Vlasenica directions with simultaneous activity by the 28th Division forces from the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, in order to cut the DK area of responsibility in two and connect the enclaves with a central part of the territory of former Bosnia-Herzegovina held by Muslim forces." This was information about activities that were carried out at the time in the territory under the control of the army, BH Army. Now, my question is: In view of this and the earlier instance where the Prosecutor said that he was not disputing that, does this mean that it was to be expected to -- that the Republika Srpska army would conduct and take such activities on in order to prevent the offensive activities in those areas where there should be no military activities? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible to take such action. That's one of the options.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, we are not requesting any additional time and I've said that I will complete my cross-examination by 2.00, but I would like to address the Trial Chamber with a request that my assistant seek to tender the documents that we wanted to tender earlier via bar table motion, in view of the fact that the Prosecutor was not disputing the facts there and these were documents that have already been admitted in other cases. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber will look forward to receive such a request by the Defence. Can I take it, Mr. Tolimir, that this concludes your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That is correct. And I would like to thank Mr. Boering and apologise to him for keeping him here under intense questioning over the course of the past two days, and I wish him a merry holiday season, the Christmas season, and I would like to thank him for coming to testify in this case. And I would also like to thank Mr. Thayer for his assistance, and I appreciate everyone's understanding. And I wish a Merry Christmas to all those who celebrate Christmas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Boering, you will be pleased to hear that now you are free to leave the Tribunal to return to your normal activities and to your home. This is really the end of your testimony in this trial. Thank you very much that you were able to come here and to stay an extended time with us in this courtroom. Thank you again. Are there any matters to raise today by either party? I don't see anybody on his feet. Mr. Boering, I would like to invite you to leave the courtroom, if you wish to do that. It concludes your testimony. Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At this point in time, I would like to express my gratitude and the gratitude of the Chamber for all those who helped us today, especially the Dutch interpreters, but the other interpreters for all the different languages as well. I would like to thank the whole staff: The Court Recorder, the Court Usher, the Court Officer, the officers of the Chamber, the Defence and the Prosecution, for their very good cooperation during the past year. Sometimes we had some problems but I think that was -- we all were able to resolve the problems after they occurred. We are grateful for this good cooperation in the courtroom, and I hope very much that we will be able to continue that way next year. We have a long time ahead in this trial. We are not sitting until the 31st of January, to enable Mr. Tolimir to review the documents, especially the diary of General Mladic. Again I would like to thank everybody and wish everybody a very happy time, good Christmastime, if you're celebrating Christmas, and a Happy New Year. See you next year. Thank you very much. We adjourn and resume on the 31st of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 31st day of January, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.03 p.m.,
